recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not rename current NutritionOrder.subject for FHIR-3707. Any future change should come from a new OO decision about group-capable NutritionOrder semantics, not from the superseded DSTU1 patient-only premise.
issue_request: FHIR-3707 was Published/Persuasive for DSTU1 and requested renaming NutritionOrder.subject to NutritionOrder.patient because only Patient was allowed and the cited naming rule says to use patient when Patient is the only reasonable subject.
initial_application: Commit 7d67ca802e5a4a4a472dcba2a975d3e1b6b9a230 applied the historical change in the old NutritionOrder spreadsheet source by changing NutritionOrder.subject to NutritionOrder.patient and adding a #3707 committee note.
additional_context: FHIR-20508 was a later Published/Persuasive R5 issue resolving that Group should be added as a NutritionOrder reference choice. It is already represented on the combined branch by no-change audit commit 30eaad627cb402bead69289b889034469b9fefb8. Commit 1a5062f0a41dca024be7fb527908dcec638166f8 then changed NutritionOrder.patient back to NutritionOrder.subject, broadened the definition to a person or set of individuals, added Group, and updated subject/patient search parameters.
reconciliation: Published empty audit commit 4e616aabdd863b997288e3b092cc5ec33388d906. The active current-build source correctly has NutritionOrder.subject as Reference(Patient|Group), maps the old NutritionOrder.patient name to NutritionOrder.subject for rename compatibility, and preserves Patient-only search via NutritionOrder.subject.where(resolve() is Patient).

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive R5 issue changed the NutritionOrder patient-only premise by requiring Group support; already audited on the combined branch as 30eaad627cb402bead69289b889034469b9fefb8.
Published global clinical-patient search-parameter issue was checked because it mentions NutritionOrder patient search behavior, but it does not require changing the NutritionOrder element name.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive DSTU1 issue requesting NutritionOrder.subject be renamed to NutritionOrder.patient because only Patient was allowed.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the historical patient-only naming decision that must be reconciled against later source history.

evidence_items.summary: The 2015 NutritionOrder spreadsheet commit changed NutritionOrder.subject to NutritionOrder.patient and added a #3707 note.
evidence_items.learned: FHIR-3707 was initially applied in the historical source.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive R5 issue asking whether NutritionOrder can be for groups, resolved to add Group as a reference choice.
evidence_items.learned: Later WG intent changed the element from patient-only to group-capable, making subject the correct current name.

evidence_items.summary: The 2022 NutritionOrder dispositions commit changed patient to subject, added Group, and rewired subject/patient search parameters.
evidence_items.learned: The current subject element is an intentional later implementation, not a forgotten FHIR-3707 regression.

evidence_items.summary: NutritionOrder is active, owned by OO, in the patient compartment, and has a legacy rename mapping from NutritionOrder.patient to NutritionOrder.subject.
evidence_items.learned: The current source is build scope and preserves compatibility for the old element name.

evidence_items.summary: NutritionOrder.subject is defined as 1..1 Reference(Patient|Group) for the person or set of individuals needing nutrition support.
evidence_items.learned: Because current NutritionOrder can target Group, the original rule points to subject rather than patient.

evidence_items.summary: The subject search parameter uses NutritionOrder.subject, while the patient search parameter is constrained to Patient references on subject.
evidence_items.learned: Search parameters are consistent with both current subject naming and Patient-specific compatibility.
